correctness.rationale: Q is invertible over finite fields, and its polynomial T^2-T-1 has distinct nonzero roots for every prime >5. In the split and nonsplit cases, diagonalization gives Q^(ell-1)=I and Q^(ell+1)=-I respectively. The two exact decompositions of pq+1 have even multiplicative factors for sign cancellation; taking matrix entries and the negative-index Fibonacci identity proves both local congruences. Chinese remaindering is exact for p≠q. A_2=A_4=0 while B_2=4, B_4=12 have no prime divisors >5; reducing characters yields p≡2 mod5, with q=p+d. For d≥6, positive fixed A_d,B_d imply p≤B_d. Modular fast doubling checks 14028 pairs as corroboration only; no infinite result rests on enumeration.

value.rationale: The recent semiprime-integral-average question naturally asks how the gap between two prime factors affects the index condition. The complete fixed-difference local residue law turns a Fibonacci number of index pq into a test involving two fixed small-index Fibonacci integers and quadratic characters. It distinguishes exactly two potentially unbounded fixed prime gaps from all larger fixed gaps, which are provably finite with explicit bounds, and identifies a sharp congruence restriction on twin/cousin-prime families. This is structurally stronger than a handful of numeric examples or an implicit restatement of divisibility; it does not claim to solve twin/cousin-prime infinitude.
